name: Chemspeed Technologies AG
subcategory: automated synthesis, formulation and gravimetric powder-dosing workstations for chemistry and materials labs
origin_detail: Swiss lab-automation company (HQ in Switzerland per its website). It says it has supported R&D and QC labs 'for over 25 years', so it was founded around 2001 or earlier; the exact year and founders were not confirmed. Bruker completed its acquisition of Chemspeed during 2024 and the company now brands itself 'Chemspeed (part of Bruker)'.
flagship_projects: Integrations with Atinary SDLabs and Bruker SciY software
openness_notes: Closed hardware designs, firmware and control software. The website mentions an 'intuitive software suite' and 'vendor-agnostic' solutions but no open APIs, open-source software or published designs. Openness is limited to integration partnerships (e.g. Atinary's SDLabs optimizer and Bruker instruments).

exit_events.note: Bruker FY2024 10-K: 'we completed our acquisition of Spectral Instruments Imaging and Chemspeed Technologies AG' during 2024; the deal 'provides us entry into lab automation and digitalization'; reported in the BSI BioSpin segment. Price, stake and exact date not found in the portions read.

risk_events: 2024: acquired by Bruker (terms not disclosed in the 10-K sections read). Bruker acquired 28 businesses in 2022-2024
Aug 2026 (approx.): Bruker announced a strategic collaboration with Atinary integrating SDLabs with Chemspeed automation, Bruker instruments and SciY software
robustness: Now backed by a large public instrument maker (Bruker revenue ~$2.96B in 2023), which reduces financial risk. All designs and software are proprietary, so users depend on Bruker's product roadmap. An active application pipeline in 2026 (349 news items on its site) signals continued investment.
physical_science_relevance: Very high. Chemspeed platforms are standard hardware in chemistry and materials SDLs. Its 2026 application news covers a self-driving lab that finds homogeneous catalysts, single-atom-catalyst libraries, rare-earth MOF crystallization mapping, North Carolina State University's academic SDL ecosystem, polymer-solvation vision models and AI-planned chemistry for b12 Foundry.
openness_effect_assessment: Chemspeed built a durable niche over 25 years with fully closed hardware and software, growing through integrations and application science rather than openness. Its 2024 sale to Bruker as Bruker's 'entry into lab automation and digitalization' shows that incumbents value closed lab-automation hardware as a strategic asset. No evidence suggests closedness held back its adoption in academic SDLs.
key_takeaway: Chemspeed is the closed-hardware counterpart to Opentrons. It is a long-lived Swiss maker of solid- and liquid-handling synthesis robots, widely used in chemistry and materials SDLs, never open, and absorbed by Bruker in 2024. Its exit was a quiet strategic acquisition, not venture hype. It now anchors a closed Bruker-Chemspeed-Atinary SDL stack (Aug 2026 collaboration), illustrating consolidation of lab automation into incumbents' proprietary ecosystems.

contradicted.note: The official company about page states the year explicitly. It is consistent with the home page's 'For over 25 years'. Null filled from the primary page.

confidence_change.reason: The 2024 Bruker acquisition is supported by the cited FY2024 10-K plus two further pages: Bruker's 2 May 2024 8-K release ('Chemspeed acquisition closed in Q1 2024') and Chemspeed's own about page ('Bruker Corporation (Nasdaq: BRKR) has acquired Chemspeed Technologies AG'). The founding year (1997) comes from the primary about page, and continued operation is shown by the Aug 2026 Bruker release. Nothing is left contradicted.

verification_pass2.note: Bruker's 13 Feb 2024 release still called Chemspeed an 'announced but not yet closed potential acquisition'; the 2 May 2024 release says it closed in Q1 2024. An XBRL context in Bruker's Q1-2024 10-Q (ChemspeedTechnologiesAGMember2024-03-06) hints at a 6 Mar 2024 closing date, but this was not stated in readable text. Stake and price are still not found. origin_detail ('founded around 2001 or earlier') is now stale given 1997. The about page says HQ relocated to Fuellinsdorf in 2017 and that Chemspeed 'remains an autonomous, vendor-agnostic business within Bruker'.
